evaluation.positioning_hook: A sheltered Lagos heiress falls for a charismatic predator with a murderous past, while her jealous cousin and a disabled brother race to stop the family from collapsing under the secret.

audience_appeal_marketability.reasoning: The core promise is legible and saleable: romance, danger, family betrayal, and a serial-killer reveal. But the script’s heightened melodramatic register and dense soap-opera plotting narrow the audience to viewers who actively want big emotional swings.

conceptual_hook_clarity.reasoning: The hook lands clearly once Presley’s predatory behavior and Kayla’s vendetta are established, especially in the bar and mansion sequences. The pilot takes a while to settle into its central engine because it opens with atmosphere and then cycles through multiple relationship threads before the danger fully locks in.

character_appeal_and_long_term_potential.reasoning: Atlanta, Kayla, Presley, and Bryan all have strong emotional positions, and the triangle/quartet has enough friction to keep generating scenes. The characters are vivid, but they are written more as operatic functions than as deeply surprising people, which limits durability without further layering.

creative_originality_and_boldness.reasoning: The Lagos setting and the family/romance/crime blend give it some identity, and Bryan’s wheelchair confinement adds a useful wrinkle. Still, the execution leans heavily on familiar soap-thriller devices: secret affairs, overheard threats, repeated flashbacks, and villain monologues.

narrative_momentum_engagement.reasoning: There is constant motion, but much of it is repetitive escalation rather than clean progression. The pilot keeps returning to the same emotional beats—warning, seduction, threat, concealment—so the forward drive is present but not especially sharp.

resonant_originality.reasoning: The premise has a recognizable hook—an innocent woman drawn into a dangerous man’s orbit—but the reveal pattern is familiar and the story telegraphs its turns early. The most distinctive element is the Lagos-family milieu, not a truly fresh structural idea.

world_density_and_texture.reasoning: The mansion world, family hierarchy, class markers, and Lagos nightlife give the series a usable social container. That said, the world mostly serves as a backdrop for private betrayals rather than a fully story-generating system with its own rules and institutions.

tonal_specificity.reasoning: The script has a consistent heightened, romantic-thriller tone, and it commits to emotional excess without apology. The downside is that the tone is broad rather than precise, so it can feel more like a melodrama with thriller elements than a sharply ownable tonal signature.

latent_depth_slow_burn_potential.reasoning: Presley’s backstory, Bryan’s confinement, and Kayla’s resentment all hint at deeper trauma and family rot beneath the surface. The pilot gestures toward that depth, but it mostly states the wounds directly instead of letting them accumulate through subtext.

relationship_density_and_ensemble_engine.reasoning: This is the script’s strongest structural asset: Atlanta/Kayla/Pamela/Shirley/Gerald/Presley/Bryan all generate conflict in different combinations. The family and lovers are entangled enough that almost any pairing produces friction, which is valuable for series longevity.

lead_characters.name: Atlanta Moe
lead_characters.demographics: Female, early 20s, affluent Lagos young woman, sheltered but emotionally hungry.
lead_characters.hook: Atlanta is the emotional center of the pilot: a romantic, impressionable young woman who wants love badly enough to ignore every warning sign. She writes the title letters, falls for Presley’s charm, and becomes the family’s most vulnerable target, which gives her a strong innocence-to-trauma arc. Her contradiction is that she reads as soft and dreamy, but the story keeps forcing her into survival mode.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of a breakout romantic-drama lead like Jurnee Smollett in Lovecraft Country or Zendaya in Euphoria when the role asks for innocence, desire, fear, and collapse in the same episode. It gives an actor the full emotional runway: longing, seduction, panic, and the final betrayal-shock turn.

lead_characters.name: Kayla Moe
lead_characters.demographics: Female, early-to-mid 30s, affluent Lagos woman, aunt-guarded family member with a volatile private life.
lead_characters.hook: Kayla is the jealous, wounded cousin whose resentment drives a major portion of the pilot’s sabotage engine. She is sexually entangled with Gerald, bitter about Atlanta’s favored status, and willing to weaponize secrets to keep control. The role has real heat because she is not just jealous; she is actively dangerous and emotionally exposed at the same time.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of volatile, morally compromised showcase that gave Jodie Comer in Killing Eve or Sarah Snook in Succession room to play charm, rage, humiliation, and threat in one performance. It offers a juicy antihero-adjacent turn with big confrontation scenes and strong scene-stealing potential.

lead_characters.name: Presley Akunde
lead_characters.demographics: Male, late 20s, wealthy Lagos man, predatory romantic lead with violent history and trauma.
lead_characters.hook: Presley is the series engine’s dark magnet: handsome, wealthy, obsessive, and increasingly monstrous, but written with enough pain to keep him from being a flat villain. He stalks Atlanta, hides murders, manipulates Bryan, and then reveals a damaged history that explains but does not excuse his violence. He is the kind of role that can carry a show if the actor can make menace feel seductive.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase lane of Penn Badgley in You or Matthew McConaughey in True Detective when the role lets an actor weaponize charisma while slowly revealing rot underneath. It gives a performer the rare opportunity to play charm, threat, remorse, and self-mythology in the same frame.

lead_characters.name: Bryan Akunde
lead_characters.demographics: Male, early-to-mid 20s, disabled, wheelchair user, wealthy family member.
lead_characters.hook: Bryan is Presley’s conscience, hostage, and witness, trapped physically and morally inside the mansion. His wheelchair is not just a detail; it defines his inability to intervene cleanly, which makes him a pressure valve for the story’s secrets. He has the makings of a tragic observer who can eventually become an active betrayer.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of emotionally loaded supporting role that gave Peter Dinklage in Game of Thrones or Rami Malek in Mr. Robot a chance to play intelligence, isolation, and moral pressure without ever leaving the room. It offers a contained but potent performance with real close-up intensity.

lead_characters.name: Pamela Moe
lead_characters.hook: Pamela is the family’s authority figure and moral center, but the script complicates her with a past tied to prostitution and control. She is protective of Atlanta, hostile to Kayla, and increasingly cornered as the household secrets spill out. She plays like a woman whose power is real but brittle.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is strong matriarch territory in the vein of Cicely Tyson in How to Get Away with Murder or Meryl Streep in Big Little Lies when the role lets an actor command a room while carrying buried shame. It gives a veteran performer confrontation scenes, grief, and authority under siege.

lead_characters.name: Shirley Moe
lead_characters.demographics: Female, mid-20s, affluent Lagos woman, cousin with asthma/inhaler dependency.
lead_characters.hook: Shirley is the more sympathetic cousin caught between attraction, loyalty, and fear. Her asthma and the inhaler detail give her a physical vulnerability that the script uses in the family conflict and the park attack sequence. She functions as both confidante and casualty, which makes her a useful emotional barometer.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of vulnerable, high-stakes supporting role that gave Auli’i Cravalho in The Power or Haley Lu Richardson in The White Lotus room to play sweetness under pressure. It offers a performer a clear emotional vulnerability and a tragic turn.

lead_characters.name: Gerald
lead_characters.demographics: Male, 30s, adult lover/kept man, socially mobile Lagos man.
lead_characters.hook: Gerald is the sexual and emotional pivot between Kayla and Shirley, and the script uses him as a catalyst for jealousy and exposure. He is not deeply shaded, but he is useful because he can be read as opportunist, lover, and accidental witness all at once. He gives the series a messy adult-romance layer outside the central murder plot.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of morally slippery romantic-support role that lets an actor do charm and self-interest in the style of Algee Smith in Euphoria or Theo James in The White Lotus. It offers a lot of reaction work and a few sharp confrontation beats.

lead_characters.name: June
lead_characters.hook: June is the household observer who knows more than she says and eventually becomes a pressure point in the family’s unraveling. She is not flashy, but she is strategically placed to carry information and witness scenes that matter. The role has utility and a grounded, working-class perspective inside the mansion’s privilege bubble.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of quietly devastating supporting role that gives an actor the same grounded authority as Sian Heder’s domestic characters or the house staff in Downton Abbey. It offers subtle reaction work, secrets, and the chance to become the audience’s eyes inside the house.

lead_characters.name: Oz
lead_characters.demographics: Male, late 20s, flirtatious Lagos socialite type.
lead_characters.hook: Oz is the flirtation engine: charming, persistent, and mostly there to complicate Shirley’s romantic and emotional choices. He is lighter than the rest of the cast, which helps the pilot breathe between heavier scenes. He also functions as a social-world marker, showing the dating ecosystem around these women.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of charismatic supporting part that lets an actor play easy charm and comic flirtation, similar to the lighter romantic energy in Insecure or Sex Education. It’s a good role for someone who can make a small part memorable.

lead_characters.name: Beatrice
lead_characters.demographics: Female, young adult, deceased in present timeline.
lead_characters.hook: Beatrice is the dead friend whose murder becomes the emotional and moral stain under Kayla’s vendetta. Even though she appears mostly in flashback and memory, she is structurally important because she gives the story a body, a grievance, and a reason for the family’s lies to harden. She is the ghost that keeps the plot moving.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is not a large role, but it is the kind of flashback part that can land hard if cast well, similar to the memory-presence roles in Mare of Easttown or Big Little Lies. It gives an actor a brief but emotionally loaded imprint.

casting_characteristics: late-20s to 30s romantic-lead casting for Presley and Gerald
young-adult female ensemble with strong beauty/glamour requirements

technical.vfx_details: Primarily stylized transitions, dreamlike dissolves, and cityscape inserts; no major creature or effects work.
technical.sfx_needs: Gunshots, blood effects, body reveals, and a few struggle beats.

platform_fit.series_engine_or_release_model: Serialized family-thriller engine with romance, murder, and betrayal driving episode-to-episode escalation.

budget.note: Contemporary, but the pilot leans on multiple mansion interiors, night exteriors, car work, and repeated stylized flashbacks; it stays scope-able, but not ultra-contained.

casting.note: Presley has to play seductive, violent, wounded, and unstable; Bryan needs a disabled performance with authority; Pamela needs matriarch gravity. The ensemble is castable, but the lead villain role is the narrowest lift.

development.note: The pilot’s central engine depends on repeated reversals around Presley, Atlanta, Kayla, and Shirley, with several flashbacks and voiceovers carrying plot information. Buyers will want clarity on the show’s primary spine versus its many overlapping betrayals.

comp_set.title: Big Little Lies
comp_set.why_it_comps: Like this pilot, it turns affluent domestic life into a pressure cooker of secrets, desire, and violence.

comp_set.title: You
comp_set.why_it_comps: The obsessive male lead, romantic predation, and voiceover-driven intimacy map cleanly to the Presley/Atlanta dynamic.

comp_set.title: How to Get Away with Murder
comp_set.why_it_comps: It shares the serialized soap-thriller energy, family secrets, and heightened reversals inside a glossy adult ensemble.

comp_set.title: Queen Sugar
comp_set.why_it_comps: The family power struggles, Black affluence, and emotional melodrama sit in a similar contemporary prestige lane.

audience_target.primary_audience: Viewers who like glossy, high-emotion relationship thrillers with betrayal, danger, and family secrets at the center.
audience_target.demographics: Adults 25-54, with a female skew and strong appeal to viewers who watch serialized domestic drama and crime-romance hybrids.

budget_tier.note: Contemporary mansion-heavy production with a few night exteriors, car scenes, and modest stunt/SFX needs; the scale is driven more by cast and schedule than by effects.

types_of_buyers: streamer development execs building adult relationship-thriller slates
indie TV producers seeking a glossy African urban setting
buyers looking for female-forward serialized soap with crime stakes
companies that package actor-driven ensemble dramas
lane_fit.detail: This sits naturally in the lane of elevated, emotionally charged streaming drama where romance and danger are equally important. The Lagos setting and affluent family ecosystem give it a marketable specificity without requiring tentpole scale.

ip_potential.detail: Standalone serialized drama; no clear spinoff vector beyond the main family ensemble.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The Presley role is a real actor trapdoor.
strengths.what_it_means: Commercially, this is the kind of seductive antagonist role that can attract a name actor or break out a new one because it asks for charm, menace, and remorse in one package. Buyers and casting directors chase this because it can anchor the whole series if the performance lands.
strengths.evidence: Presley’s scenes with Atlanta shift from flirtation and gift-giving to the bedroom assault and then to the breakdown after the gunshot.

strengths.what_it_means: This gives the series multiple playable pairings, which is valuable for episodic story generation and for marketing the show as a family-pressure cooker. Streamers and producers like ensembles that can sustain multiple emotional engines without needing a new case every week.
strengths.evidence: Atlanta/Kayla/Pamela/Shirley/Gerald/Bryan all collide in different combinations across the mansion, bar, bedroom, and park scenes.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The Lagos setting gives the show a specific lane.
strengths.what_it_means: The city and its affluent social world provide a recognizable but underused backdrop for a glossy adult thriller, which helps the project stand out in a crowded domestic-drama market. Buyers looking for African urban stories with premium polish will notice that immediately.
strengths.evidence: The pilot repeatedly frames Lagos city lights, mansion interiors, beachside scenes, and nightlife spaces as part of the story’s visual identity.

strengths.dimension_or_area: Bryan adds a strong moral witness function.
strengths.what_it_means: A disabled brother trapped inside the villain’s house is a useful long-term pressure point because he can carry secrets, guilt, and eventual betrayal without leaving the core setting. That kind of contained witness role is attractive to actors and helps the series keep tension inside the family system.
strengths.evidence: Bryan watches Presley’s crimes, is confined to a wheelchair, and eventually helps expose him.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The show has a clean emotional engine.
strengths.what_it_means: At its core, the series is about desire turning into danger, which is an easy buyer pitch and a reliable audience promise. That clarity helps marketing because the hook is immediate even before the plot details are explained.
strengths.evidence: Atlanta falls for Presley, Kayla resents Atlanta, and Presley’s violence turns the romance into a survival story.

whats_special.headline: This is a glossy, actor-forward streaming thriller with a seductive villain role, a volatile family ensemble, and a Lagos setting that gives the material a distinct market identity. It’s the kind of serialized melodrama a buyer can understand fast and package around performance, not spectacle.

items.area: The pilot repeats the same danger beat.
items.detail: A lot of the hour cycles through the same pattern: Presley charms Atlanta, a warning arrives, someone panics, then the story resets into another confrontation. That keeps the energy high on the page, but it also makes the escalation feel circular rather than cumulative.

items.area: The voiceover carries too much plot.
items.detail: Atlanta, Kayla, Presley, and Bryan all narrate key turns, and several flashbacks are explained more through voice than through action. Buyers will notice that the emotional intent is clear, but the pilot leans heavily on explanation to move the story forward.

items.area: Presley’s trauma backstory arrives in blocks.
items.detail: The stepmother/sterility/abuse material gives him motivation, but it is delivered in a dense explanatory dump after the assault rather than seeded with more restraint. That makes the character legible, though it also reduces the mystery and can flatten the reveal impact.

items.area: Kayla’s villainy is broad and explicit.
items.detail: Her threats, jealousy, and sexual entanglements are all stated very directly, which makes her easy to read but less layered than the script seems to want. A producer would flag that the role is playable, but the writing currently leans more toward declaration than subtext.

issues.headline: The main friction is structural: the pilot keeps returning to warnings, seduction, and threats instead of building a cleaner escalation path. The other buyer concern is that the script explains its characters’ wounds very directly, which makes the emotional stakes clear but reduces the sense of discovery.
